findings.issue: The Forward bullet says stepping off means 'one Back leaves the app' unconditionally. After a reload on the Table and Resume ([app, T1old, T2*]), Back pauses onto T1old, Forward steps off T2 back onto T1old, and leaving the app then takes two Backs. That matches D-3 (foreign entries keep today's behaviour) and the reload paragraph below, but the bullet reads as universal.

summary: All SPEC items are implemented and their tests catch real breakage. I ran mutations in an isolated copy of the repo (scratchpad, working tree untouched). (a) Removing the tableWritesSettled guard (SPEC-03) fails SPEC-01 and SPEC-02 in both Chromium and WebKit with 'Received: ... 0 hands · paused'. (b) Removing the step-off fails SPEC-06 in both browsers. (c) Going back to the timeOrigin+counter key fails SPEC-04 and history.spec case (5) in both browsers. With the real code, --repeat-each=5 over pause-history, history, error-recovery, home-control and rebuy gave 210/210 passes in 33.6 s: no flakes under the paused clock. The step-off can't loop: back() from lastTableKey lands on a null or foreign entry, and the popstate there is ignored because its key is not lastTableKey. It only acts when tableKey.current is null, and no screen shows a Table with a null tableKey: openTable sets the key, and closeTable/popstate-pause clear it only when leaving. Return Home (TASK-13.1) remounts App on Home with tableKey null. The module-level lastTableKey survives the remount, so a later Forward still steps off. A popstate from AppRoot's own back() carries a null or foreign state and is ignored. The hold wraps IDBDatabase.prototype.transaction, matches only the armed sessions-only readwrite (putSession), keeps it open with a count() chain that issues no timers, and releases by ending the chain. It is test-only (nothing imported from src/). The key uses crypto.getRandomValues(16 bytes) as hex. The locked history.spec.ts edit only removes the { pausedClock: false } option and the timeOrigin comment; the case body is unchanged apart from re-indentation. Only NIT findings.
